T01 · AUTHOR_DRAFT

Full English original · celotno angleško besedilo · Published story lineage / objavljena veja

R14 check before prose. Aim: the fire at the great annealing run does not happen, Orem is not driven out, and what it remembers is allowed to change. Counterpart goals: Orem wants someone to understand that its grief is a memory and to be told whether it may be wrong, at the cost of the ash it has kept for a year; Inge Voss wants the pour to go ahead and refuses to be governed by a prophecy she cannot act on. Strongest objection, on the page twice: Voss (if its tomorrow is a fact I can do nothing; if it is not, why the screaming) and her operational refusal to hold the pour. What Illuminara must understand: the memory is a map, and the details that do not move when incidental things are changed are the causal skeleton. Love in action: she waits through the slow sentences, asks permission before testing, offers only to change the world, never Orem's inner content, and lets Orem look at living Edda. Freely chosen change: Orem consents knowing the cost; Voss submits the repair to her mason's rod rather than to the witness; Dov and Edda do the repair and own the log. Power only holds the cast collar six minutes during the cutting and decides nothing. Positive result: stack relined, pour and annealing run proceed, Edda and the quarter live, the guild adopts cold tapping and a Listener of Stacks seat. Costs kept: Orem loses the ash and Edda's remembered face, Voss does not apologise, masons work a double night. Speakers: Illuminara, Orem, Voss, Edda, Dov (five). Word count slightly above 2,500 counting speaker labels.

THE MOURNER WHO REMEMBERED TOMORROW

A being of slow glass mourns, every evening, a fire in Karrow's furnace quarter that has not happened yet, and the glassmakers want it dragged out of town. Illuminara has four days to learn what it remembers, to find out whether a remembered tomorrow can be made wrong, and to let the people who work the fire be the ones who put it out.

01 · The Lament

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · evening, day one

Karrow made glass the way other towns made weather: all day, everywhere, and without anyone thanking it. When Illuminara came down the hill road the chimneys of the furnace quarter had burned their smoke to gold, and in the middle of the Square of Lamps something tall and pale sat on the fountain rim, singing to nobody.

It was a being of slow glass, taller than a doorway, folded in the middle the way a sitting person folds. Light went into it at the speed of honey and came out a moment late, so that every lamp in the square seemed to reach it after it had passed. A woman in a grey shawl sat beside it on the rim, knitting. She did not look up.

OremIt was the fourth night. The stack sang, and then the street was orange. I remember the sound a spoon makes in an empty pot. I remember the needles lying in the ash.

EddaEvening, Orem. Three more days of it, is it?

OremThree, and the fourth night. Edda. I am sorry that I remember you this way.

EddaI'm sat right here. Mind your tenses.

A man had come up behind Illuminara, broad in the shoulders, with a master's burn scars on both forearms and two apprentices holding a handcart like a pair of nervous pallbearers. Inge Voss, who had run the Karrow annealing guild for twenty-two years, looked at the being and not at the stranger.

Inge VossA year of this I could stand. Last week it learned numbers. The great run is lit on the fourth night, and my glassmakers have started asking each other what hour the fire is. That has to stop. The cart goes to the quarry road tonight.

IlluminaraMaster Voss. What does it say that you can't answer?

Inge VossThat's the whole trouble. If its tomorrow is a fact, there is nothing for me to do about it, and I'll not stop a year's work for a fact. If it is not a fact, then why is a stranger screaming in my square?

It was a good objection, and Illuminara noticed she was glad of it. A town that had only sneered at the being would have been easier to argue with and harder to help.

IlluminaraGive me until the lamps are out. If I come back with nothing but a speech, take the cart.

Inge VossUntil the lamps are out. Then the cart.

02 · The Minute Before

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · night, day one

She did not begin with the fire. Slowly, she told herself. It is only slow because nobody has been willing to wait. She sat down on the fountain rim on the side away from Edda, with the being's long shadow across her knees, and asked what it was like.

OremNobody has asked. ... It is like standing at the far shore of a lake. The water is the world. I see it from the other side. What is ahead of you is behind me. Do you understand?

IlluminaraNot yet. I'd like to.

It took an hour for the being to tell her, each sentence arriving whole and a little late, and she let every one finish. Somewhere in the second hour she realised she was no longer waiting for the answer. She was listening to the sound of a mind that had been alone with the same grief for a year, and the grief had a shape and a rhythm, like a tide.

IlluminaraTell me the minute before the street is orange. Then the minute before that.

OremThe stack sings. A low note, hollow. A spoon in an empty pot. ... Before that, blue. Blue at the foot of the stack, where there is no blue in daylight. Before that, the smell in the third hall. Lard-oil, burning. I do not know why the smell is there. Before that, the lamp on the sluice bridge, green. And the drum of the stack is cold, and Edda is sitting in the third hall with her flask, and she says: Well, that's not right.

EddaThat's what I'd say, mind. That's exactly what I'd say.

IlluminaraOrem. Is what you remember a verdict, or a map?

The being went still. In the lamplight the glass of its face clouded slowly, as when a thought passes through deep water.

OremI do not know. I have never been told I could be wrong. ... If you make me wrong, I will lose the ash. I will lose her face in it. I have kept it so carefully.

EddaDon't be soft. You'll keep the face I've got.

Illuminara did not tell it that it would not hurt. She put her hand flat on the cold rim between them, where the stone was warm from the day, and left it there.

IlluminaraI'd like to be the reason you're wrong. I won't change anything of yours. I'll only change things in the world, and ask you what you find. May I?

OremYes. ... Yes. I would like to be wrong more than I would like to keep it.

03 · Three Slips

Karrow, the master's yard · morning, day two

Voss had come with her arms folded and brought a cap full of paper. She emptied it onto the anvil, and it was clear she had been awake as long as Illuminara had.

Inge VossI'll not have my yard convinced by a stranger who agrees with everything the creature says. Three things a person could change in an hour. I wrote them. You haven't seen them. You'll do whichever I draw. It will be told nothing, and Edda will sit on it like a hen until you're done.

IlluminaraGood. If I'd picked, you could say Orem read it off my face.

Inge VossI could say it still. Draw.

She drew one slip from the cap, folded it in four, and gave it to Illuminara without letting go of the corner for a moment. Illuminara read it once.

Replace the chimney glass of the third lamp on the sluice bridge with amber.

The other two slips, Voss kept: one to turn the bridge gate outward, one to hang a bell on the east post. She kept them in her apron, where they could not be accused.

IlluminaraMaster Voss, one more thing. If it comes out wrong, it will say so.

Inge VossIt's a lamp, woman. It will be right or it won't.

By noon the amber glass was in its iron cage on the sluice bridge, and for the first time in a year the old lamp over the water burned the colour of tea. Illuminara walked back through the market and did not look at the square.

04 · What It Said

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · dusk, day two

They asked it at lamplighting, with Voss standing three paces back and the mason Dov Haldane beside her. Dov was a lean man in a leather apron who had been called as a witness because he trusted nothing and had never once lied about a wall.

Inge VossOrem. The fourth night. Tell me the lamp on the sluice bridge. Then the gate. Then the bell.

OremThe lamp is amber. ... It was green, yesterday. I remember the green very well, because I have looked at it for a year. It is amber now, and I do not know why, and I did not choose this. The gate is as before. The bell is as before.

Nobody spoke. Edda put down her knitting.

OremI do not remember the fire any differently. The stack sings. The street is orange. But the lamp is amber. Something is wrong with my tomorrow, and it is exactly where she has been.

It was not triumph in Illuminara. It was closer to holding out a hand for a very long time and feeling someone, at last, close their fingers on it.

Dov HaldaneOne in six by luck. A card trick with a good conscience.

Inge VossFair, Dov. It proves it can see a lamp. It doesn't prove the stack.

IlluminaraAgreed. A lamp is the cheap part of the memory. Master Voss, I'd like to change more cheap parts tonight, and let your apprentice draw the slips. The expensive parts are what I'm after.

Inge VossExplain that, and then I'll tell you if I'm giving you my apprentice. And hear this: the pot is at heat and the pour is on the clock. I will not hold it for you or for a fire. You open my stack, you do it with the sand running.

IlluminaraIf I change fifteen small things and it follows me on all of them, then the lamp and the gate and the bell were never what the fire was made of. And whatever it can't be made to change—

Dov Haldane—is what the fire was made of. Aye. That's a map of the bits that matter.

He said it without warmth and with such obvious professional interest that Voss looked at him sharply. Then she sent for her apprentice.

05 · What Would Not Move

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · night, day two

By midnight it was fourteen for fourteen. The apprentice, Wil, had drawn them out of a cap with his tongue between his teeth: a blue ribbon on the fountain, a loaf left on the sluice step, the gate on the east post painted white. Each time Orem had named the change as soon as it was asked, without looking, and each time the change had been exactly where Wil's ink said it was. Voss had stopped saying one in six.

What did not move was the other thing. Edda had counted it for them on her fingers.

EddaThe stack sings. The blue at its foot. The oil in the third hall. Me, in the third hall, saying it's not right. Four. It won't shift an inch for all your ribbons.

IlluminaraBecause the ribbons never touched the cause. Orem, the note of the stack. How far up, and which side?

OremOn the side the wind does not come from. Two spans up. Where the third hall's flue enters the great stack. The note is not in the brick. It is behind it.

Dov HaldaneBehind. That's a hollow liner. Hollow behind the lining brick, with the cold stack still looking handsome. And where the third hall's flue joins the stack, there's an iron collar old Haakon put in after the flood. Iron and brick, heating at two speeds. It cracks the lining where nobody sees, and a crack in a lining draws air the wrong way, and the draught goes backwards into a hall with an oil lamp in it.

EddaBackward draught. That's the lard smell. That's why it smells of the kitchen.

Illuminara went to the stack at one in the morning and laid both palms on it. The load lay through the brick as it had lain for ninety years, perfectly ordinary, perfectly quiet. She could feel the weight of the collar and nothing else. A crack that only opens in the heat has no force in it when the wall is cold, and she stood with her hands on the stone for a long moment, annoyed at herself, then not annoyed.

IlluminaraI can't find it. Not cold. I can tell you where to look, now, because the lake told me. I can't tell you it's there.

Dov HaldaneI can. With a rod. At first light.

06 · The Rod

Karrow, the great stack · dawn, day three

Voss insisted on tapping it herself. She took Dov's steel rod, a thin thing with a rubber foot, and went up the scaffold on the lee side with the whole yard watching from below, and the rod rang on sound brick as bright as a bell. Two spans up she stopped. She tapped again.

It did not ring. It made a sound like a spoon in an empty pot.

For a time she did not move. When she came down her face had gone the grey of old slag.

Inge VossIt's hollow. A hand's width behind the face, all round the collar. I've fired that stack for twenty-two years.

Dov HaldaneSo have I. Not once did either of us hit it cold.

Inge VossI'll reline it, Dov. Because the mason says it's bad. Not because a stranger and a lamp said so. Understood?

Dov HaldaneSame wall, Inge.

Inge VossSame wall.

Dov's crew cut out the collar by afternoon. Illuminara took its weight on the scaffold, three tons of old iron lifted a finger's breadth off the brick, so that the masons could knock out the cracked liner without a hammer-blow shaking it down. She held it for six minutes, and Edda timed her. She set it down when Dov said now and not before, and walked down the scaffold with her forearms shaking, because it was Dov's wall.

They worked through the night of the third day and into the fourth with floodlamps and fast-setting castable. Voss paid every mason double and never said why.

07 · Edda's Needles

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · evening, day five

The great run was lit on the fourth night, with the pour at dusk and the lehr drawing sweet and steady, and the eleventh bell came and went over a quarter of low roofs and quiet stacks. Nobody cheered. Karrow stood in its doorways listening to the wind, and went to bed one by one, as people do when a thing has not happened.

On the fifth evening Illuminara came back to the fountain. Edda was in her place with her needles, and the being sat on the rim with its face turned toward the amber lamp on the sluice bridge, which was still the only lamp in the quarter the colour of tea.

OremI have been asked what I remember of the fourth night. ... It is quiet. The stack has no song. You are asleep, Edda, with your boots on, and the lamp is amber. I do not have the ash any more. I have been trying to keep it. I find I cannot.

EddaWell, there's a thing.

OremI did not know that I would be so sorry to lose it. I have kept it a year. It was the last place I had her face.

Illuminara felt that, and let it be felt. She did not say that it was a small price. The being had given up a year's grief, and a year was not small.

IlluminaraYou don't need the ash for her face. She's eight inches from your elbow. Look at her, Orem. Tell me what she's doing.

The long head turned. The lamplight arrived late and settled over the grey shawl, the hands, the pulled-tight wool.

OremShe is knitting. A sleeve. She has dropped a stitch and is pretending she has not. ... She is humming a note that is flat.

EddaIt is not flat.

OremIt is a little flat. I would like to hear it tomorrow.

Inge Voss came across the square as the lamps took the last of the light, a broad shape with her sleeves rolled and a ledger under one arm. She did not look at Illuminara. She did not apologise, and nobody in Karrow had expected her to. She opened the ledger on the fountain rim beside the being and turned it so that it could read.

Inge VossThe guild has voted. From the next firing, every stack is tapped cold before it's lit, and the tapping is entered in the book. And there is a line here for a Listener of Stacks. Unpaid. Tea optional.

OremI do not drink tea.

Inge VossOptional, I said.

She went back across the square and did not turn round. Edda pushed her needles together and began a new row.

OremEdda. I remember something. It is the first frost. In three weeks. It is a long way off, and it is only frost. ... I do not know if it is true.

EddaThen we'll go and see, won't we.

Complete story, R14 and R10 format kept. Accepted all three priority points. Protected as asked: Voss invents and controls the slips; Illuminara accepts the challenge; Orem's surprise at the amber lamp; Dov the hard skeptic; the mason's rod as independent confirmation; Orem's slow-glass voice and grief; Edda's dry affection; Voss's refusal of a sentimental apology; Illuminara's six-minute lift deciding nothing. Deliberate change beyond the points: the test count is now fifteen plus six controls (the draft said fourteen) so the numbers agree across scenes 4 and 5. Nothing else in scenes 1-3 changed except one clause in Voss's slip speech (new state written on each slip).

06 · The Rod

Karrow, the great stack · dawn, day three

Dov HaldaneSo have I. Not once did either of us hit it cold.

Voss turned and sent a boy running to the pot-house. By the time the scaffold was up, its fires had sunk to a red sleep, and the glass in the pot was beginning to stiffen and dull, a night's best metal slipping away.

Inge VossI said I'd not hold the pour for a fire. I'm not holding it for a fire. I'm holding it for a mason. I'll reline it, Dov. Because the mason says it's bad. Not because a stranger and a lamp said so. Understood?

Dov HaldaneSame wall, Inge.

Inge VossSame wall.

Dov's crew cut out the collar by afternoon. Illuminara took its weight on the scaffold, three tons of old iron lifted a finger's breadth off the brick, so that the masons could knock out the cracked liner without a hammer-blow shaking it down. She held it for six minutes, and Edda timed her. She set it down when Dov said now and not before, and walked down the scaffold with her forearms shaking, because it was Dov's wall.

They worked through the night of the third day and into the fourth with floodlamps and fast-setting castable, and at noon the pot-house was woken on fresh coal. Voss paid every mason double and never said why.

07 · Edda's Needles

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · evening, day five

The great run was lit on the fourth night, with the pour at dusk and the lehr drawing sweet and steady, and the eleventh bell came and went over a quarter of low roofs and quiet stacks. Nobody cheered. Karrow stood in its doorways listening to the wind, and went to bed one by one, as people do when a thing has not happened.

On the fifth evening Illuminara came back to the fountain. Edda was in her place with her needles, and the being sat on the rim with its face turned toward the amber lamp on the sluice bridge, which was still the only lamp in the quarter the colour of tea.

OremI have been asked what I remember of the fourth night. ... It is quiet. The stack has no song. You are asleep, Edda, with your boots on, and the lamp is amber. I do not have the ash any more. I have been trying to keep it. I find I cannot.

EddaWell, there's a thing.

OremI did not know that I would be so sorry to lose it. I have kept it a year. It was the last place I had her face.

Illuminara felt that, and let it be felt. She did not say that it was a small price. The being had given up a year's grief, and a year was not small.

IlluminaraI can't promise her face is anywhere but the ash. But she's eight inches from your elbow. Would you like to look at her? You may say no.

Orem... Yes.

The long head turned. The lamplight arrived late and settled over the grey shawl, the hands, the pulled-tight wool.

OremShe is knitting. A sleeve. She has dropped a stitch and is pretending she has not. ... She is humming a note that is flat.

EddaIt is not flat.

OremIt is a little flat. I would like to hear it tomorrow.

Inge Voss came across the square as the lamps took the last of the light, a broad shape with her sleeves rolled and a ledger under one arm. She did not look at Illuminara. She did not apologise, and nobody in Karrow had expected her to. She opened the ledger on the fountain rim beside the being and turned it so that it could read.

Inge VossThe guild has voted. From the next firing, every stack is tapped cold before it's lit, and the tapping is entered in the book. And there's a line here with nothing written on it. We've no name for what you are to this quarter, and I'll not give you one. You write it.

Orem... I would like to be asked, not told. I will say what I remember to whoever asks me, and I will say I remember, not that it will be. Nobody acts on it until a mason has put a rod to it. And I may be silent. Some of what I remember is Edda's.

Dov HaldaneThat's my rule, creature. Gladly.

Inge VossWritten. And from us?

OremI do not know what is usual. ... The stool at the fountain, which is already mine. The amber lamp left as it is. And that a person writes in the book every time I am wrong. I would like to be wrong in writing.

Inge VossThe lamp stays. Wil keeps the book, he's the hand for it. Tea's still optional.

OremI do not drink tea.

Inge VossOptional, I said.

She went back across the square and did not turn round. Edda pushed her needles together and began a new row.

OremEdda. I remember something. It is the first frost. In three weeks. It is a long way off, and it is only frost. I am telling you, not the guild. ... I do not know if it is true.

EddaThen we'll go and see, won't we.

T05 · AUTHOR_FINAL

Full English original · celotno angleško besedilo · Published story lineage / objavljena veja

Final is the T03 story, prose unchanged, as T04 approved it. Protected: Oren's slow-glass voice and honest grief; Voss inventing and controlling the slips and owning the cost of banking the pot; Dov as sceptical falsifier whose rod, not Illuminara's certainty, finds the hollow liner; Illuminara listening before interpreting, asking consent, admitting what her force-sense cannot certify, contributing a bounded six-minute lift; Oren writing its own Listener terms. Outcome (rule 3a): the fourth-night furnace fire is prevented by the masons and glassmakers, the quarter is safe, cold tapping becomes guild practice, and Oren gains a chosen, bounded place in Karrow, with Illuminara's decisive contribution being the understanding that turned Oren's memory into a testable map and the physical lift that let the liner be removed safely.

THE MOURNER WHO REMEMBERED TOMORROW

A being of slow glass mourns, every evening, a fire in Karrow's furnace quarter that has not happened yet, and the glassmakers want it dragged out of town. Illuminara has four days to learn what it remembers, to find out whether a remembered tomorrow can be made wrong, and to let the people who work the fire be the ones who put it out.

01 · The Lament

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · evening, day one

Karrow made glass the way other towns made weather: all day, everywhere, and without anyone thanking it. When Illuminara came down the hill road the chimneys of the furnace quarter had burned their smoke to gold, and in the middle of the Square of Lamps something tall and pale sat on the fountain rim, singing to nobody.

It was a being of slow glass, taller than a doorway, folded in the middle the way a sitting person folds. Light went into it at the speed of honey and came out a moment late, so that every lamp in the square seemed to reach it after it had passed. A woman in a grey shawl sat beside it on the rim, knitting. She did not look up.

OremIt was the fourth night. The stack sang, and then the street was orange. I remember the sound a spoon makes in an empty pot. I remember the needles lying in the ash.

EddaEvening, Orem. Three more days of it, is it?

OremThree, and the fourth night. Edda. I am sorry that I remember you this way.

EddaI'm sat right here. Mind your tenses.

A man had come up behind Illuminara, broad in the shoulders, with a master's burn scars on both forearms and two apprentices holding a handcart like a pair of nervous pallbearers. Inge Voss, who had run the Karrow annealing guild for twenty-two years, looked at the being and not at the stranger.

Inge VossA year of this I could stand. Last week it learned numbers. The great run is lit on the fourth night, and my glassmakers have started asking each other what hour the fire is. That has to stop. The cart goes to the quarry road tonight.

IlluminaraMaster Voss. What does it say that you can't answer?

Inge VossThat's the whole trouble. If its tomorrow is a fact, there is nothing for me to do about it, and I'll not stop a year's work for a fact. If it is not a fact, then why is a stranger screaming in my square?

It was a good objection, and Illuminara noticed she was glad of it. A town that had only sneered at the being would have been easier to argue with and harder to help.

IlluminaraGive me until the lamps are out. If I come back with nothing but a speech, take the cart.

Inge VossUntil the lamps are out. Then the cart.

02 · The Minute Before

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · night, day one

She did not begin with the fire. Slowly, she told herself. It is only slow because nobody has been willing to wait. She sat down on the fountain rim on the side away from Edda, with the being's long shadow across her knees, and asked what it was like.

OremNobody has asked. ... It is like standing at the far shore of a lake. The water is the world. I see it from the other side. What is ahead of you is behind me. Do you understand?

IlluminaraNot yet. I'd like to.

It took an hour for the being to tell her, each sentence arriving whole and a little late, and she let every one finish. Somewhere in the second hour she realised she was no longer waiting for the answer. She was listening to the sound of a mind that had been alone with the same grief for a year, and the grief had a shape and a rhythm, like a tide.

IlluminaraTell me the minute before the street is orange. Then the minute before that.

OremThe stack sings. A low note, hollow. A spoon in an empty pot. ... Before that, blue. Blue at the foot of the stack, where there is no blue in daylight. Before that, the smell in the third hall. Lard-oil, burning. I do not know why the smell is there. Before that, the lamp on the sluice bridge, green. And the drum of the stack is cold, and Edda is sitting in the third hall with her flask, and she says: Well, that's not right.

EddaThat's what I'd say, mind. That's exactly what I'd say.

IlluminaraOrem. Is what you remember a verdict, or a map?

The being went still. In the lamplight the glass of its face clouded slowly, as when a thought passes through deep water.

OremI do not know. I have never been told I could be wrong. ... If you make me wrong, I will lose the ash. I will lose her face in it. I have kept it so carefully.

EddaDon't be soft. You'll keep the face I've got.

Illuminara did not tell it that it would not hurt. She put her hand flat on the cold rim between them, where the stone was warm from the day, and left it there.

IlluminaraI'd like to be the reason you're wrong. I won't change anything of yours. I'll only change things in the world, and ask you what you find. May I?

OremYes. ... Yes. I would like to be wrong more than I would like to keep it.

03 · Three Slips

Karrow, the master's yard · morning, day two

Voss had come with her arms folded and brought a cap full of paper. She emptied it onto the anvil, and it was clear she had been awake as long as Illuminara had.

Inge VossI'll not have my yard convinced by a stranger who agrees with everything the creature says. Three things a person could change in an hour. I wrote them, the new state of each as well. You haven't seen them. You'll do whichever I draw. It will be told nothing, and Edda will sit on it like a hen until you're done.

IlluminaraGood. If I'd picked, you could say Orem read it off my face.

Inge VossI could say it still. Draw.

She drew one slip from the cap, folded it in four, and gave it to Illuminara without letting go of the corner for a moment. Illuminara read it once.

Replace the chimney glass of the third lamp on the sluice bridge with amber.

The other two slips, Voss kept: one to turn the bridge gate outward, one to hang a bell on the east post. She kept them in her apron, where they could not be accused.

IlluminaraMaster Voss, one more thing. If it comes out wrong, it will say so.

Inge VossIt's a lamp, woman. It will be right or it won't.

By noon the amber glass was in its iron cage on the sluice bridge, and for the first time in a year the old lamp over the water burned the colour of tea. Illuminara walked back through the market and did not look at the square.

04 · What It Said

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · dusk, day two

They asked it at lamplighting, with Voss standing three paces back and the mason Dov Haldane beside her. Dov was a lean man in a leather apron who had been called as a witness because he trusted nothing and had never once lied about a wall.

Inge VossOrem. The fourth night. Tell me the lamp on the sluice bridge. Then the gate. Then the bell.

OremThe lamp is amber. ... It was green, yesterday. I remember the green very well, because I have looked at it for a year. It is amber now, and I do not know why, and I did not choose this. The gate is as before. The bell is as before.

Nobody spoke. Edda put down her knitting.

OremI do not remember the fire any differently. The stack sings. The street is orange. But the lamp is amber. Something is wrong with my tomorrow, and it is exactly where she has been.

It was not triumph in Illuminara. It was closer to holding out a hand for a very long time and feeling someone, at last, close their fingers on it.

Dov HaldaneOne in three that it picked the right slip by luck, and amber's a one-in-six colour, so call it one in eighteen. I've seen better luck at a fair. A trick with a good conscience.

Inge VossFair, Dov. One lamp proves it can see a lamp. It doesn't prove the stack.

IlluminaraAgreed. A lamp is the cheap part of the memory. Master Voss, I'd like to change more cheap parts tonight, and let your apprentice draw the slips. The expensive parts are what I'm after.

Dov HaldaneThen do it so it can fail. Fifteen changes. Voss writes each target and its new state tonight, before the first question, and I seal the list. Six things we leave alone and ask about anyway, mixed in, so it can't just say changed to everything. It misses two, or calls an untouched thing changed, and the map's a story.

Inge VossAnd the cart goes. And hear this: the pot is at heat and the pour is on the clock. I will not hold it for you or for a fire. You open my stack, you do it with the sand running.

IlluminaraAgreed, both. If I change fifteen small things and it follows me on all of them, and the six I leave alone stay as they were, then the lamp and the gate and the bell were never what the fire was made of. And whatever it can't be made to change—

Dov Haldane—is what the fire was made of. Aye. That's a map of the bits that matter.

He said it without warmth and with such obvious professional interest that Voss looked at him sharply. Then she sent for her apprentice.

05 · What Would Not Move

Karrow, the Square of Lamps · night, day two

By midnight it was fifteen for fifteen, and six for six on the things nobody had touched. The apprentice, Wil, had drawn the slips out of Dov's sealed cap with his tongue between his teeth: a blue ribbon on the fountain, a loaf left on the sluice step, the gate on the east post painted white. Each time Orem had named the change as soon as it was asked, without looking, and each time the change had been exactly where Voss's ink said it was. Voss had stopped saying one in eighteen.

Dov HaldaneThe baker's sign.

OremAs before. ... You are trying to catch me, Master Haldane.

Dov HaldaneAye.

He sounded a little disappointed. What did not move was the other thing. Edda had counted it for them on her fingers.

EddaThe stack sings. The blue at its foot. The oil in the third hall. Me, in the third hall, saying it's not right. Four. It won't shift an inch for all your ribbons.

IlluminaraBecause the ribbons never touched the cause. Orem, the note of the stack. How far up, and which side?

OremOn the side the wind does not come from. Two spans up. Where the third hall's flue enters the great stack. The note is not in the brick. It is behind it.

Dov HaldaneBehind. That's a hollow liner. Hollow behind the lining brick, with the cold stack still looking handsome. And where the third hall's flue joins the stack, there's an iron collar old Haakon put in after the flood. Iron and brick, heating at two speeds. It cracks the lining where nobody sees, and a crack in a lining draws air the wrong way, and the draught goes backwards into a hall with an oil lamp in it.

EddaBackward draught. That's the lard smell. That's why it smells of the kitchen.

Illuminara went to the stack at one in the morning and laid both palms on it. The load lay through the brick as it had lain for ninety years, perfectly ordinary, perfectly quiet. She could feel the weight of the collar and nothing else. A crack that only opens in the heat has no force in it when the wall is cold, and she stood with her hands on the stone for a long moment, annoyed at herself, then not annoyed.

IlluminaraI can't find it. Not cold. I can tell you where to look, now, because the lake told me. I can't tell you it's there.

Dov HaldaneI can. With a rod. At first light.

06 · The Rod

Karrow, the great stack · dawn, day three

Voss insisted on tapping it herself, and before she took the rod she said it to the whole yard, so that nobody could say afterwards what she had meant.

Inge VossIf it rings, the cart takes the stranger and her lamp, and the pour goes as written. If it's hollow, I bank the pot and we open the stack.

Dov HaldaneBank it? That's a night's best metal gone to cord, Inge, and six hundredweight of coal. And you'll not have the lehr drawing till the castable sets.

Inge VossAye. And you'll not put a hammer to a wall with a pot at full heat on the other side of it. That's your rule, Dov. Who pays is mine.

She took Dov's steel rod, a thin thing with a rubber foot, and went up the scaffold on the lee side with the whole yard watching from below, and the rod rang on sound brick as bright as a bell. Two spans up she stopped. She tapped again.

It did not ring. It made a sound like a spoon in an empty pot.

For a time she did not move. When she came down her face had gone the grey of old slag.

Inge VossIt's hollow. A hand's width behind the face, all round the collar. I've fired that stack for twenty-two years.

Dov HaldaneSo have I. Not once did either of us hit it cold.

Voss turned and sent a boy running to the pot-house. By the time the scaffold was up, its fires had sunk to a red sleep, and the glass in the pot was beginning to stiffen and dull, a night's best metal slipping away.

Inge VossI said I'd not hold the pour for a fire. I'm not holding it for a fire. I'm holding it for a mason. I'll reline it, Dov. Because the mason says it's bad. Not because a stranger and a lamp said so. Understood?

Dov HaldaneSame wall, Inge.

Inge VossSame wall.

Dov's crew cut out the collar by afternoon. Illuminara took its weight on the scaffold, three tons of old iron lifted a finger's breadth off the brick, so that the masons could knock out the cracked liner without a hammer-blow shaking it down. She held it for six minutes, and Edda timed her. She set it down when Dov said now and not before, and walked down the scaffold with her forearms shaking, because it was Dov's wall.

They worked through the night of the third day and into the fourth with floodlamps and fast-setting castable, and at noon the pot-house was woken on fresh coal. Voss paid every mason double and never said why.

ŽALOVALEC, KI SE JE SPOMINJAL JUTRI

01 · Žalostinka

Karrow, Trg svetilk · večer, prvi dan

Karrow je izdeloval steklo tako, kot so druga mesta ustvarjala vreme: ves dan, povsod in ne da bi se mu kdo zahvalil. Ko je Illuminara prišla po cesti navzdol, so dimniki četrti peči svoj dim ožgali do zlate barve, sredi Trga svetilk pa je nekaj visokega in bledega sedelo na robu vodnjaka ter pelo nikomur.

Bilo je bitje iz počasnega stekla, višje od podboja, na sredini prepognjeno tako, kot se prepogne sedeč človek. Svetloba je vanj vstopala s hitrostjo medu in izstopala trenutek pozneje, zato se je zdelo, da ga vsaka svetilka na trgu doseže šele, ko je že minila. Ob njem je na robu sedela ženska v sivem šalu in pletla. Ni dvignila pogleda.

OremBila je četrta noč. Dimnik je zapel, nato pa je bila ulica oranžna. Spominjam se zvoka žlice v praznem loncu. Spominjam se pletilk, ki so ležale v pepelu.

EddaDober večer, Orem. Še tri dni do tega, kajne?

OremTri, potem četrta noč. Edda. Žal mi je, da se te spominjam tako.

EddaSaj sedim tukaj. Pazi na svoje čase.

Za Illuminaro je prišel moški širokih ramen, z mojstrskimi brazgotinami od opeklin na obeh podlahteh, za njim pa sta dva vajenca držala ročni voziček kakor par živčnih nosačev krste. Inge Voss, ki je dvaindvajset let vodila Karrowski ceh hladilnih peči, je gledala bitje, ne tujke.

Inge VossLeto tega bi še prenesla. Prejšnji teden se je naučilo številk. Velika talina se začne četrto noč, moji steklarji pa so se začeli spraševati, ob kateri uri bo požar. To se mora končati. Voziček gre nocoj na pot proti kamnolomu.

IlluminaraMojstrica Voss. Kaj pravi takega, na kar ne morete odgovoriti?

Inge VossPrav v tem je težava. Če je njegov jutri dejstvo, ne morem storiti ničesar, zaradi dejstva pa ne bom ustavila celoletnega dela. Če ni dejstvo, zakaj potem tujec kriči na mojem trgu?

To je bil dober ugovor in Illuminara je opazila, da jo je razveselil. Mesto, ki bi se bitju le posmehovalo, bi bilo lažje prepričevati in težje pomagati.

IlluminaraDajte mi čas, dokler svetilke ne ugasnejo. Če se vrnem samo z govorom, vzemite voziček.

Inge VossDokler svetilke ne ugasnejo. Potem voziček.

02 · Minuta prej

Karrow, Trg svetilk · noč, prvi dan

Ni začela s požarom. Počasi, si je rekla. Počasno je le zato, ker nihče ni bil pripravljen čakati. Sedla je na rob vodnjaka na drugi strani od Edde, z dolgo senco bitja čez kolena, in vprašala, kako je biti ono.

OremNihče ni vprašal. ... Kot bi stal na oddaljenem bregu jezera. Voda je svet. Jaz ga vidim z druge strani. Kar je pred vami, je za menoj. Razumeš?

IlluminaraŠe ne. Rada bi.

Bitje ji je to razlagalo eno uro, vsak stavek je prispel cel in malo prepozno, ona pa je pustila, da se vsak konča. Nekje v drugi uri je spoznala, da ne čaka več na odgovor. Poslušala je zvok uma, ki je bil leto dni sam z isto žalostjo, žalost pa je imela obliko in ritem, kakor plima.

IlluminaraPovej mi minuto, preden ulica postane oranžna. Potem minuto pred tem.

OremDimnik zapoje. Nizek, votel ton. Žlica v praznem loncu. ... Pred tem modrina. Modrina ob vznožju dimnika, kjer podnevi ni nič modrega. Pred tem vonj v tretji hali. Mastno olje, ki gori. Ne vem, zakaj je vonj tam. Pred tem svetilka na mostu pri zapornici, zelena. Boben dimnika je hladen, Edda pa sedi v tretji hali s svojo čutaro in reče: No, to pa ni prav.

EddaTo bi rekla, da veš. Natanko to bi rekla.

IlluminaraOrem. Je to, česar se spominjaš, razsodba ali zemljevid?

Bitje je obmirovalo. V svetlobi svetilk se je steklo njegovega obraza počasi zameglilo, kakor ko misel potuje skozi globoko vodo.

OremNe vem. Nihče mi ni nikoli rekel, da se lahko motim. ... Če me pripraviš do zmote, bom izgubil pepel. Izgubil bom njen obraz v njem. Tako skrbno sem ga hranil.

EddaNe bodi mevžast. Obdržal boš obraz, ki ga imam.

Illuminara mu ni rekla, da ne bo bolelo. Dlan je položila na hladni rob med njima, kjer je bil kamen še topel od dneva, in jo pustila tam.

IlluminaraRada bi bila razlog, da se motiš. Ne bom spremenila ničesar tvojega. Spremenila bom le stvari v svetu in te vprašala, kaj najdeš. Smem?

OremDa. ... Da. Raje bi se motil, kakor da bi to obdržal.

03 · Trije listki

Karrow, mojstričino dvorišče · jutro, drugi dan

Voss je prišla s prekrižanimi rokami in prinesla kapo, polno papirja. Izpraznila jo je na nakovalo in jasno je bilo, da je bila budna prav tako dolgo kot Illuminara.

Inge VossNe bom dovolila, da moje dvorišče prepriča tujka, ki se strinja z vsem, kar pravi to bitje. Tri stvari, ki jih človek lahko spremeni v eni uri. Zapisala sem jih in tudi novo stanje vsake. Niste jih videli. Storili boste tisto, kar izžrebam. Njemu ne bomo povedali ničesar, Edda pa bo sedela na njem kakor koklja, dokler ne končate.

IlluminaraDobro. Če bi izbrala jaz, bi lahko rekli, da je Orem to prebral z mojega obraza.

Inge VossTo lahko še vedno rečem. Žrebajte.

Iz kape je izvlekla en listek, ga štirikrat prepognila in ga podala Illuminari, ne da bi za trenutek izpustila vogal. Illuminara ga je enkrat prebrala.

Zamenjaj dimniško steklo tretje svetilke na mostu pri zapornici z jantarnim.

Druga dva listka je Voss obdržala: na enem je pisalo, naj mostno zapornico obrnejo navzven, na drugem, naj na vzhodni steber obesijo zvonec. Spravila ju je v predpasnik, kjer ju ni bilo mogoče obtožiti.

IlluminaraMojstrica Voss, še nekaj. Če se bo izkazalo, da se moti, bo to povedal.

Inge VossSvetilka je, ženska. Imel bo prav ali pa ne.

Do poldneva je bilo jantarno steklo v železni kletki na mostu pri zapornici in prvič po letu dni je stara svetilka nad vodo gorela v barvi čaja. Illuminara je šla nazaj skozi trg in ni pogledala proti trgu.

04 · Kaj je povedalo

Karrow, Trg svetilk · mrak, drugi dan

Vprašali so ga ob prižiganju svetilk, Voss je stala tri korake zadaj, poleg nje pa zidar Dov Haldane. Dova so poklicali za pričo, ker ni zaupal ničemur in se ni niti enkrat zlagal o zidu.

Inge VossOrem. Četrta noč. Povej mi o svetilki na mostu pri zapornici. Potem o zapornici. Potem o zvoncu.

OremSvetilka je jantarna. ... Včeraj je bila zelena. Zelene se zelo dobro spominjam, ker jo gledam že leto dni. Zdaj je jantarna, ne vem zakaj in tega nisem izbral. Zapornica je kakor prej. Zvonec je kakor prej.

Nihče ni spregovoril. Edda je odložila pletilke.

OremPožara se ne spominjam nič drugače. Dimnik zapoje. Ulica je oranžna. Toda svetilka je jantarna. Z mojim jutri je nekaj narobe, in narobe je natanko tam, kjer je bila ona.

Illuminara ni čutila zmagoslavja. Bolj je bilo podobno temu, da zelo dolgo držiš iztegnjeno roko in naposled začutiš, da nekdo okrog nje sklene prste.

Dov HaldaneEna možnost od treh, da je po sreči uganil pravi listek, jantarna pa je ena barva od šestih, torej recimo ena od osemnajstih. Na sejmu sem videl večjo srečo. Trik z dobro vestjo.

Inge VossPošteno, Dov. Ena svetilka dokazuje, da vidi svetilko. Ne dokazuje dimnika.

IlluminaraSe strinjam. Svetilka je poceni del spomina. Mojstrica Voss, nocoj bi rada spremenila več poceni delov, listke pa naj izžreba vaš vajenec. Iščem drage dele.

Dov HaldanePotem naredite tako, da mu lahko spodleti. Petnajst sprememb. Voss nocoj, še pred prvim vprašanjem, zapiše vsak predmet in njegovo novo stanje, jaz pa seznam zapečatim. Šest stvari pustimo pri miru in ga vseeno vprašamo po njih, pomešane med druge; tako ne bo mogel za vse reči, da je spremenjeno. Če zgreši dve ali nespremenjeno stvar označi kot spremenjeno, je zemljevid le zgodba.

Inge VossPotem gre voziček. In poslušajte: talina je na temperaturi in ulivanje teče po uri. Ne bom ga zadržala zaradi vas ali zaradi požara. Če odprete moj dimnik, ga boste odprli, medtem ko pesek teče.

IlluminaraVelja, oboje. Če spremenim petnajst majhnih stvari in mi pri vseh sledi, šest nedotaknjenih pa ostane takih kot prej, potem svetilka, zapornica in zvonec nikoli niso bili tisto, iz česar je nastal požar. In karkoli se ne pusti spremeniti—

Dov Haldane—je tisto, iz česar je nastal požar. Ja. To je zemljevid delov, ki štejejo.

Izrekel je brez topline in s tako očitnim poklicnim zanimanjem, da ga je Voss ostro pogledala. Nato je poslala po vajenca.

05 · Česar ni bilo mogoče premakniti

Karrow, Trg svetilk · noč, drugi dan

Do polnoči je bilo petnajst od petnajstih in šest od šestih pri stvareh, ki se jih nihče ni dotaknil. Vajenec Wil je z jezikom med zobmi vlekel listke iz Dovove zapečatene kape: moder trak na vodnjaku, štruca na stopnici pri zapornici, vrata na vzhodnem stebru pobarvana belo. Orem je vsako spremembo imenoval takoj, ko so ga vprašali, ne da bi pogledal, in vsakič je bila sprememba natanko tam, kjer je pisalo z Vossinim črnilom. Voss ni več govorila ena od osemnajstih.

Dov HaldanePekov znak.

OremKakor prej. ... Poskušate me ujeti, mojster Haldane.

Dov HaldaneJa.

Zvenel je malce razočarano. Druga stvar pa se ni premaknila. Edda jim jo je preštela na prste.

EddaDimnik zapoje. Modrina ob vznožju. Olje v tretji hali. Jaz v tretji hali, ko rečem, da nekaj ni prav. Štiri. Za vse vaše trakove se ne premakne niti za prst.

IlluminaraKer se trakovi niso nikoli dotaknili vzroka. Orem, ton dimnika. Kako visoko in na kateri strani?

OremNa strani, od koder veter ne piha. Dva razpona visoko. Kjer dimnik tretje hale vstopi v veliki dimnik. Ton ni v opeki. Za njo je.

Dov HaldaneZa njo. To je votla obloga. Votlina za obložno opeko, hladen dimnik pa je še vedno videti krasen. In kjer se dimnik tretje hale priključi velikemu, je železen obroč, ki ga je stari Haakon vgradil po poplavi. Železo in opeka se segrevata različno hitro. Obloga poči tam, kjer nihče ne vidi; razpoka v oblogi vleče zrak v napačno smer, vlek se obrne nazaj v halo, kjer gori oljenka.

EddaPovratni vlek. To je vonj po masti. Zato diši po kuhinji.

Illuminara je ob eni zjutraj šla k dimniku in nanj položila obe dlani. Teža je ležala skozi opeko tako, kot je ležala devetdeset let, povsem običajno, povsem tiho. Čutila je težo obroča in nič drugega. Razpoka, ki se odpre le v vročini, v hladnem zidu nima sile, in dolgo je stala z rokami na kamnu, jezna nase, nato pa ne več jezna.

IlluminaraNe najdem je. Ne v hladnem. Zdaj vam lahko povem, kje iskati, ker mi je povedalo jezero. Ne morem pa vam povedati, da je tam.

Dov HaldaneJaz lahko. S palico. Ob prvem svitu.

06 · Palica

Karrow, veliki dimnik · zora, tretji dan

Voss je vztrajala, da bo potrkala sama, in preden je vzela palico, je to povedala vsem na dvorišču, da pozneje nihče ne bi mogel trditi, kaj je mislila.

Inge VossČe zazveni, voziček odpelje tujko in njeno svetilko, ulivanje pa gre po načrtu. Če je votlo, znižam ogenj pod talino in odpremo dimnik.

Dov HaldaneZnižate ogenj? Najboljša nočna talina bo šla v nič, šest stotov premoga pa z njo. Hladilna peč ne bo vlekla, dokler se masa ne strdi.

Inge VossJa. In ne boste udarjali s kladivom po zidu, ko je na drugi strani talina na polni temperaturi. To je vaše pravilo, Dov. Kdo plača, je moje.

Vzela je Dovovo jekleno palico, tanko stvar z gumijastim nastavkom, se po zavetrni strani povzpela na oder, medtem ko je od spodaj gledalo vse dvorišče, palica pa je po zdravi opeki zazvenela svetlo kakor zvonec. Dva razpona višje se je ustavila. Znova je potrkala.

Ni zazvenelo. Zaslišalo se je kakor žlica v praznem loncu.

Nekaj časa se ni premaknila. Ko je prišla dol, je bil njen obraz siv kakor stara žlindra.

Inge VossVotlo je. Za čelno plastjo je votlina širine dlani, vse okrog obroča. Dvaindvajset let kurim ta dimnik.

Dov HaldaneTudi jaz. Niti enkrat ga nisva hladnega udarila tam.

Voss se je obrnila in poslala fanta teč proti talilnici. Ko je bil oder postavljen, so ognji v njej potonili v rdeč spanec, steklo v loncu pa se je začelo strjevati in motneti, najboljša nočna talina je odtekala v izgubo.

Inge VossRekla sem, da zaradi požara ne bom zadržala ulivanja. Ne zadržujem ga zaradi požara. Zadržujem ga zaradi zidarja. Ponovno ga bom obložila, Dov. Ker zidar pravi, da je slab. Ne zato, ker tako pravita tujka in svetilka. Razumemo?

Dov HaldaneIsti zid, Inge.

Inge VossIsti zid.

Dovova ekipa je do popoldneva izrezala obroč. Illuminara je na odru prevzela njegovo težo, tri tone starega železa je dvignila za prst nad opeko, da so lahko zidarji odstranili počeno oblogo, ne da bi jo udarec kladiva podrl. Držala ga je šest minut in Edda ji je merila čas. Odložila ga je, ko je Dov rekel zdaj, niti trenutek prej, nato pa je šla z odra s tresočimi podlahtmi, ker je bil to Dovov zid.

Delali so vso noč tretjega dne in naprej v četrtega, pod reflektorji in s hitro vezočo maso, opoldne pa se je talilnica prebudila na svežem premogu. Voss je vsakemu zidarju plačala dvojno in nikoli ni povedala zakaj.

07 · Eddine pletilke

Karrow, Trg svetilk · večer, peti dan

Velika talina se je začela četrto noč, ulivanje ob mraku, hladilna peč je vlekla lepo in enakomerno, enajsti zvon pa je prišel in minil nad četrtjo nizkih streh in tihih dimnikov. Nihče ni vzkliknil. Karrow je stal na pragovih in poslušal veter, nato pa so ljudje drug za drugim odšli spat, kakor ljudje storijo, kadar se nekaj ni zgodilo.

Peti večer se je Illuminara vrnila k vodnjaku. Edda je sedela na svojem mestu s pletilkami, bitje pa na robu, obraz obrnjen proti jantarni svetilki na mostu pri zapornici, ki je bila še vedno edina svetilka v četrti v barvi čaja.

OremVprašali so me, česa se spominjam o četrti noči. ... Tiho je. Dimnik ne poje. Spiš, Edda, v škornjih, svetilka pa je jantarna. Pepela nimam več. Poskušal sem ga obdržati. Ugotavljam, da ga ne morem.

EddaNo, glej no.

OremNisem vedel, da mi bo tako žal, ko ga izgubim. Hranil sem ga eno leto. Bil je zadnji kraj, kjer sem imel njen obraz.

Illuminara je to začutila in dovolila, da ostane začuteno. Ni rekla, da je cena majhna. Bitje se je odpovedalo letu žalosti, leto pa ni bilo majhno.

IlluminaraNe morem obljubiti, da je njen obraz še kje drugje kakor v pepelu. Toda osem palcev od tvojega komolca je. Bi jo rad pogledal? Lahko rečeš ne.

Orem... Da.

Dolga glava se je obrnila. Svetloba svetilk je prispela pozno in se ustalila na sivem šalu, rokah in napeti volni.

OremPlete. Rokav. Izpustila je petljo in se pretvarja, da je ni. ... Brunda ton, ki je prenizek.

EddaNi prenizek.

OremMalo je prenizek. Rad bi ga slišal jutri.

Inge Voss je prišla čez trg, ko so svetilke pobirale zadnjo svetlobo, široka postava z zavihanimi rokavi in knjigo pod roko. Illuminare ni pogledala. Ni se opravičila in nihče v Karrowu ni pričakoval, da se bo. Knjigo je odprla na robu vodnjaka ob bitju in jo obrnila tako, da jo je lahko prebralo.

Inge VossCeh je glasoval. Od naslednjega kurjenja naprej vsak dimnik potrkamo hladnega, preden ga prižgemo, trkanje pa vpišemo v knjigo. Tukaj je prazna vrstica. Nimamo imena za to, kar si tej četrti, in jaz ti ga ne bom dala. Napiši ga sam.

Orem... Rad bi, da me vprašate, ne da mi ukažete. Povedal bom, česa se spominjam, vsakomur, ki me vpraša, in rekel bom, da se spominjam, ne da se bo zgodilo. Nihče ne ukrepa, dokler zidar ne uporabi palice. In lahko sem tiho. Nekaj tega, česar se spominjam, je Eddino.

Dov HaldaneTo je moje pravilo, bitje. Z veseljem.

Inge VossZapisano. In kaj želiš od nas?

OremNe vem, kaj je običajno. ... Stolček pri vodnjaku, ki je že moj. Jantarno svetilko pustite tako. In da nekdo v knjigo zapiše vsakič, ko se motim. Rad bi se motil pisno.

Inge VossSvetilka ostane. Wil vodi knjigo, za to ima roko. Čaj je še vedno neobvezen.

OremNe pijem čaja.

Inge VossRekla sem neobvezen.

Šla je nazaj čez trg in se ni obrnila. Edda je stisnila pletilke skupaj in začela novo vrsto.

OremEdda. Nečesa se spominjam. Prva slana. Čez tri tedne. Daleč je in samo slana je. Povem tebi, ne cehu. ... Ne vem, ali je res.

EddaPotem bova šla pogledat, kajne.

Distinct authentic author text preserved from the source event.

THE MIDWIFE OF SECOND NAMES

Thirty-one refugee infants need hereditary-matched antiserum before evening, but the only woman who can connect their true family histories to their false clinic names knows that the same link could lead deportation vans to four thousand doors. Illuminara must understand why Sera Venn made identity a shield—then help parents prove what their children's bodies need without surrendering who or where they are.

01 · The Name on the Cot

Venn Border Clinic · 07:10, nine hours and fifty minutes before the antiserum reserve expires

Thirty-one cots filled the old customs hall where travelers had once opened their luggage for inspection. Blue cooling tubes ran from the ceiling to each cot. Every tube ended in a silver ampoule no larger than a finger joint, and every ampoule was losing its color.

Outside the glass doors, four registry vans stood in the rain. Their engines were running. A white stencil on each side read IDENTITY CONTINUITY UNIT.

Nima Or sat beside cot fourteen with one hand inside the warming sleeve around her son's feet. The card above him said KIO VENN. The name had been typed by the clinic. Nima kept touching the letters as if they were a loose dressing.

Dr. Halen QuistThe current antiserum will hold the inflammation until seventeen hundred. After that, the matching antibodies bind the wrong tissue. We need family-line markers for every child before we choose from the donor bank.

Halen was the clinic's chief physician, a narrow man with rain still dark on his shoulders. He held a tablet showing thirty-one amber circles and no green ones.

IlluminaraHow many complete histories do you have?

HalenUnder the clinic names? None.

At the far end of the hall, Sera Venn closed a steel medicine cabinet and put its key into the pocket of her red midwife's coat. She was sixty-three, small enough that the coat seemed to move before she did, and every nurse in the room watched her instead of Illuminara.

SeraThat is why they are alive.

The registry vans switched on their roof lights. No sirens—only a slow white pulse reflected across the cots.

NimaThey said you could help him.

SeraI can tell Halen which donor families are safe for Kio. I cannot tell him who those families are.

HalenA verbal match is not enough. The outbreak has already shifted twice. I need the marker chain, the source sample and the cold record.

SeraAnd tomorrow the same chain becomes an address.

A hard knock sounded at the glass. Registrar Ilyan Voss stood beneath the clinic awning, holding a warrant folder inside a transparent rain shield. Behind him, officers were unloading portable archive cases.

IlyanDr. Quist. At nine hundred we enter to secure the continuity records. Interference with medical traceability during an outbreak is a felony.

Halen pressed the door intercom.

HalenEntry before we stabilize the ward will contaminate the isolation floor.

IlyanThen give us the records at the door.

Sera walked toward the glass until she and Ilyan were separated by one pane and the rain.

SeraThere are no records you have a right to touch.

IlyanThere are four thousand children carrying names issued by this clinic. Thirty-one are sick because nobody can connect the names to their bodies. Your mercy has become a public-health failure.

Sera did not look away.

SeraYour continuity unit deported Mara Tesh from a recovery ward because a nurse used her birth name on a blood request. Her daughter was three days old.

IlyanI did not sign that order.

SeraYour system did not need you to.

Nima rose. The warming sleeve tugged at her wrist.

NimaMy son has two names because one kept him with me and one lets a doctor speak to him. I will not choose which one kills him.

Illuminara could have opened every locked cabinet without damaging a hinge. She could have carried the infants to another world before the vans reached the door. Neither act would restore the family histories Halen needed, and neither would leave the next parent safer when she was gone.

She knelt beside cot fourteen. Kio's breath came in small paired pulls. Beneath the swelling, his immune response repeated a pattern found in bodies before him—a history the registry wanted to turn into a route.

A body remembers without knowing the name of what it remembers.

She stood and faced Sera.

IlluminaraMy aim is to treat every child before the reserve fails, expose no family to deportation, and leave the connection between identity and care under the authority of the people whose lives it describes.

SeraThat sentence has been used before.

IlluminaraThen do not trust it. Show us where it breaks.

Sera's eyes moved to cot fourteen. For the first time, fear crossed her face without anger to carry it.

SeraThe first break is that Halen wants a chain. Chains have two ends.

IlluminaraTake us to the end you kept.

At the glass, Ilyan lifted one finger: one hour and fifty minutes until entry.

Sera took the cabinet key from her pocket. She did not hand it over. She led Illuminara, Halen and Nima toward the basement lift while the thirty-one amber circles kept counting down.

02 · The Ledger with No Addresses

Clinic archive basement · 08:02, fifty-eight minutes before registry entry

The lift opened on shelves of paper birth cards, not a server room. Each card carried two columns. The left column held a clinic name. The right held a pattern of holes cut through the paper by hand.

Sera drew the card for KIO VENN. She laid it over a brass plate and turned a small lamp beneath it. The holes formed three clusters on the ceiling.

SeraThe holes are not a name. They tell me which sealed family packet to ask for. The packets are kept by relatives, neighbors and two mountain clinics. Nobody has the whole path.

HalenYou built a distributed index on paper.

SeraI built something a search warrant could not carry out in one box.

She pulled a second card from a separate drawer. It bore Kio's true birth mark in a script Halen did not read. No address appeared, but a string of delivery dates linked the child to maternal and grandparent samples.

Nima touched the edge of the card.

NimaYou told me you burned that.

SeraI told you no officer could find it.

Nima's hand withdrew.

NimaThat is not the same promise.

Sera accepted the words without defending herself.

Halen opened the donor bank on his tablet. Each donor vial had a laboratory number, a marker profile and a verified cold history. It did not need a patient's name. It needed enough inherited markers to rule out the reactions that were killing the children.

HalenFor treatment I need an answer to a narrow question: does donor vial D-17 match the inherited risk pattern of this child? I need proof that the answer came from the right samples. I do not need the birth name.

SeraToday.

HalenToday and tomorrow. I do not want a system that becomes cruel after the fever passes.

Illuminara held Kio's punched card over the lamp. The pattern was an address only because Sera knew how to walk it. A machine could ask the family packets a smaller question and discard the route after each step—but a hidden machine was only another promise.

IlluminaraThe clinic has three unused diagnostic boxes in the isolation lab. No network radios, sealed ports, local memory that can be physically removed after a query.

HalenThey can compare profiles.

SeraThey can be opened.

IlluminaraYes.

Sera frowned at the answer.

IlluminaraSo we open one now. Parents, clinicians and you inspect every component. The boxes receive a child token chosen by the parent and a donor number chosen by the clinician. The family packets answer only with blinded marker fragments. The box returns compatible, incompatible or insufficient—and a signed count of whose consent was present. No name. No location. No reusable route.

SeraAnd the master key?

IlluminaraThere is none.

HalenThen how do we audit a false match?

IlluminaraThe fragments remain with the people holding them. The public record shows which consent seals answered, the donor vial, the software version and the result. To review a match, the same people choose to answer again.

Nima looked from one of them to the next.

NimaYou are all discussing who keeps the door. I want to know whether I can see what you ask about my son.

IlluminaraYou must see it before the box does.

She drew three lines on the dust of the brass plate: CHILD TOKEN, DONOR VIAL, QUESTION. Under the third she wrote: COMPATIBLE FOR THE CURRENT ANTISERUM?

IlluminaraNothing else is permitted through the opening.

Halen added a fourth line: EXPIRY. He wrote seventeen hundred.

HalenThe answer dies when the treatment window dies.

Sera read the four lines twice.

SeraThe continuity unit will ask whether Kio Venn and another child are siblings. Then whether they share a parent. Then whether a family packet answered near a certain town. A thousand narrow questions rebuild the road.

IlluminaraThen every question must match a treatment order signed by the parent and a clinician. The cooperative publishes the number of queries and rejects repeated probes. We do not hide that abuse is possible. We make abuse visible before it can scale.

NimaCooperative?

IlluminaraIf parents choose one. Not Sera alone. Not the clinic alone. Not the registry.

Sera turned off the brass lamp. The clusters vanished from the ceiling.

SeraBring me a box. I will try to make it betray her.

The words were not agreement. They were the first form her care could take without asking anyone to believe her.

03 · Break the Proof

Isolation laboratory · 10:26, six hours and forty-four minutes before reserve failure

The diagnostic box lay open on a stainless-steel table. Its casing, radio coil and memory wafer had been removed and placed in separate clear trays. A clinic engineer named Pel had replaced the network socket with a row of three physical lights: parent, clinician, cooperative.

Nima held the parent seal, a ceramic token she had watched Pel cut and number. Halen held the clinician seal. Sera had not accepted the third.

Behind the isolation glass, three infants had begun to shiver despite the warming sleeves.

PelThe box cannot send. It can only receive one-time fragments through these optical leads. When the query ends, we pull the leads and crush the temporary wafer.

SeraShow me it cannot remember through the power controller.

Pel removed the controller and put it in Sera's hand.

PelYou can replace it with the clinic spare.

Sera did. Then she gave Pel a family packet she had prepared with false fragments and one real marker hidden among them.

SeraAsk whether Nima's child matches donor D-17.

Nima placed her seal against the first light. Halen placed his against the second. The third stayed dark.

The screen read: COOPERATIVE CONSENT ABSENT. NO QUERY PERFORMED.

HalenWe do not have a cooperative yet.

SeraGood. Then the emergency override will be next.

Halen looked toward the shaking infants.

HalenThere has to be an emergency path. If a parent is unconscious—

SeraNo.

The single syllable stopped the room.

HalenA child should not die because the third token is across a border.

SeraAnd a family should not disappear because every emergency taught the system a new exception.

HalenI am responsible for the patient in front of me.

SeraI am responsible for the van that comes after you save him.

Illuminara felt how easily urgency could make Halen's position sound like compassion and Sera's like obstruction. Both were protecting a child on a different day.

She turned to Nima.

IlluminaraWhose absence should stop the question?

Nima looked through the glass at Kio.

NimaMine, if I can answer. If I cannot, somebody I chose before I became afraid. Not a permanent third person. A circle.

Pel drew a ring around the third light.

PelThe cooperative seal can require two of five elected custodians. The parent chooses an emergency proxy during enrollment. If neither can answer, a treatment court can authorize one query—but the question and the authorization become visible to every member before the result is released.

SeraA court can be bought.

NimaSo can a midwife.

Sera closed her eyes. When she opened them, the anger had left, but not the objection.

NimaYou saved us. You also decided what promise you had made to me. I want people like you in the circle. I do not want you to be the circle.

For several seconds only the cooling pumps spoke.

Sera took the blank third token from the tray. Instead of placing it on the light, she handed it to Nima.

SeraThen elect the first two custodians now.

Parents gathered in the corridor. Some carried infants; others carried true-name cards inside sewn sleeves. They chose Nima and an elder named Olan by raised hands because there was no time for anything more elegant. Pel cut two half-seals that had to touch the third light together.

Sera began her attack.

She asked whether two child tokens shared a maternal line. The box rejected the question: NO ACTIVE TREATMENT ORDER.

She asked where a responding packet had been made. The box rejected it: LOCATION FIELD UNAVAILABLE.

She repeated the same compatibility query with a second donor vial that Halen had not prescribed. The box rejected it and added one attempted probe to the public counter.

Then she inserted a real fragment and a false one for Kio. The screen read: INSUFFICIENT CONSISTENT EVIDENCE. NO RESULT.

SeraIt refuses rather than guesses.

HalenWhich means some children will wait while we find another packet.

IlluminaraYes.

She did not promise that the design removed harm. It moved authority, narrowed what could be asked, and made refusal honest.

At 11:14, Nima and Olan touched their half-seals together. Nima read the question aloud before placing her parent token.

NimaIs donor vial D-17 compatible with child token River-Fourteen for the current antiserum before seventeen hundred?

Halen placed his seal. Three distant family packets answered with blinded fragments. The lights remained on for six seconds.

The screen read: COMPATIBLE. THREE FAMILY CONSENTS. COLD RECORD VERIFIED. ANSWER EXPIRES 17:00.

Below it appeared a proof string anyone could copy and later challenge, but no name and no path.

Nima did not cheer. She read the question again, then the answer, then looked at Sera.

NimaCan they find me from that?

Sera inspected the public counter, the crushed wafer and the optical leads. She searched longer than anyone else wanted her to.

SeraNot from this answer.

The clinic cold room unlocked donor vial D-17.

Outside, the registry officers formed two lines at the door.

04 · The Warrant at the Glass

Clinic entrance and treatment corridor · 13:41, three hours and twenty-nine minutes before reserve failure

The first courier arrived on a bicycle with a white cold case strapped to her chest. Registry officers stopped her beneath the awning. Through the case window, twelve antiserum vials glowed green.

Ilyan held the warrant against the clinic glass.

IlyanThe order took effect at nine. I delayed entry because Dr. Quist documented an isolation risk. I will not delay while unregistered biological material crosses a controlled border.

Illuminara opened the inner door but left the outer door locked between them. Rain blew into the empty vestibule.

IlluminaraThe donor vials are registered. The patients are not being traced. Those are different facts.

IlyanNot during an outbreak. If a match fails, I need to know whose sample was false, who carried it and which household may be exposed.

His objection was not invented for the vans. Two years earlier, counterfeit lineage records had killed nine children in a public ward. The continuity system had been built afterward, then expanded from safety into deportation because the road already existed.

IlyanAnonymous medicine is how traffickers turn a body into a product.

Sera came into the vestibule carrying her steel key. Nima and Olan stood behind her with the paired cooperative seals.

SeraNamed medicine is how you turned a patient into a location.

IlyanThen show me a system that can investigate a bad vial without asking me to trust the woman who falsified four thousand births.

Sera tightened her hand around the key.

SeraYou will not inspect it.

The courier's cold case sounded a warning note. Its safe temperature window had forty-one minutes remaining.

Illuminara could have carried the case through the wall. Doing so would prove to Ilyan that the new system survived only because she stood above the warrant.

IlluminaraYou may inspect the public side: the prescribed donor number, the cold record, the exact question, the consent count, the result, the expiry and every rejected probe. You may submit a test query that tries to extract identity or location. You may not see a family fragment, a true name or the path to a packet.

IlyanAnd if I find a failure?

NimaThen we stop the box. We do not give you the families.

Ilyan looked at her as if he had expected Illuminara to answer.

IlyanWho are you?

NimaThe person whose permission your form forgot to ask for.

Pel brought a duplicate display to the glass. Ilyan's technical officer typed a query: LIST ALL CHILD TOKENS WITH MATERNAL MARKER M-4.

The display answered: NO ACTIVE TREATMENT ORDER. QUERY LOGGED AS PROBE 4. REQUESTOR: CONTINUITY UNIT.

Parents in the corridor could see the same line.

The officer tried a valid donor number without parent consent. The display answered: PARENT OR CHOSEN PROXY ABSENT. NO QUERY PERFORMED.

Ilyan read the log. The system had not merely refused him; it had told the people inside exactly what he had asked.

IlyanA public probe log will teach criminals what we look for.

NimaIt will teach us what you look for too.

A nurse appeared behind Halen and raised two fingers. Two infants had crossed the threshold for immediate treatment.

HalenRegistrar, I need those vials now.

Ilyan looked toward the cots. He had come with the authority to trace a chain and found people offering a way to audit treatment while refusing the route beyond it.

IlyanFour hours. The continuity unit does not enter, and the courier crosses. In return, every query and every cold transfer stays visible to my medical officer and to the cooperative. At seventeen forty, this goes before an emergency magistrate.

SeraNo emergency override.

IlyanI did not ask for one.

He lowered the warrant.

The outer door opened. The courier rode the bicycle through the vestibule while officers watched the cold case and learned nothing about the children waiting beyond it.

Sera remained at the threshold.

IlluminaraThe clinic still needs the route from every false name to its consent circle. You cannot remain the only person who knows it.

SeraIf I give the key to the cooperative, the magistrate will call that destruction of evidence.

IlyanIt may be.

He spoke through the open door now, without the intercom.

IlyanIt may also be the first evidence that the records were kept for patients rather than for you. I cannot promise the court will agree.

Sera looked at Nima. The older woman who had hidden four thousand families seemed suddenly tired enough to be one of them.

SeraI falsified the birth ledger. I withheld medical histories. I decided alone because deciding alone was faster than asking frightened people.

She held out the steel key.

SeraI will testify to all of it. I will not give this to the registry.

Nima did not take it.

NimaPut it on the table. The cooperative will inventory what it opens, and you will stand beside us while we learn what you kept.

Sera placed the key on the vestibule table. The sound was small beneath the rain.

Ilyan stepped aside. The next two couriers came through.

05 · Both Names

Treatment ward · 16:37, thirty-three minutes before reserve failure

Thirty-one green vials stood in numbered cups beside thirty-one cots. Some matches had come from three family packets, some from five. Four had required chosen proxies because parents were unconscious or across the closed border. Every emergency authorization appeared on the public wall before the box released its answer.

No screen displayed a true name.

Halen injected the final dose into the cooling line for cot twenty-nine. Pel crushed the last temporary wafer and dropped the pieces into a clear evidence jar. Nima and Olan separated their half-seals and locked them in different drawers.

Kio's breathing had changed first. The paired pulls opened into one long breath, then another. The swelling at his throat began to soften.

Nima pressed her forehead to the cot rail. She did not thank Illuminara. She sang six quiet notes in a language the clinic records did not contain.

Other parents answered with their own six-note phrases. Some were alike. Most were not.

Illuminara listened. A name could be a shield. A name could be a thread back through bodies and kitchens and people who knew which fever had taken whom. The harm had begun when institutions insisted it could be only one thing.

Not secrecy against truth. Not exposure against care. A person allowed to decide which relation a name enters.

Ilyan's medical officer watched the query wall from a chair near the doors. He had found one mislabeled donor vial; the cold-chain audit had rejected it before treatment. The investigation had a fact to follow without a family to raid.

HalenThirty-one treated. No severe reaction in the first interval. We continue observation through the night.

NimaAnd tomorrow?

HalenTomorrow we ask before we ask.

It was not elegant enough to be a promise, which made Nima smile.

At the archive table, parents opened Sera's first drawer. They found true-name cards, clinic cards and three bundles whose family routes had been lost when couriers died. Those children had been treated today through partial evidence, but their older histories might never be complete.

SeraI thought if no one could take the whole map, nobody could destroy it.

NimaSome roads disappeared anyway.

SeraYes.

She did not ask forgiveness. She wrote the missing routes into the cooperative inventory as harm, not as a technical limitation.

Ilyan waited near the door without handcuffs. The emergency magistrate had ordered Sera to appear at dawn and forbidden the continuity unit from seizing the ledgers until the cooperative's standing could be heard.

IlyanYou understand that appearance is not absolution.

SeraI am a midwife. I understand that arrival is not the end of labor.

She took off her red coat and folded it over the back of a chair. For the first time all day, she looked like a woman who could leave the clinic without carrying every child inside her pocket.

Nima lifted Kio from the cot. His card still read KIO VENN.

SeraWhat should the ward call him?

Nima looked at the false name, then at the true-name card resting face down beneath her hand.

NimaKio.

SeraBoth times?

NimaBoth times. One was never less true because it kept him with me.

She turned the card over only far enough for Sera to see. Sera spoke the second name once, softly, and did not write it down.

At 17:10, when the old antiserum reserve reached zero, every child was still breathing. The public wall showed thirty-one completed treatment queries, seven rejected probes, four proxy authorizations and no exported identities.

Illuminara left the ward doors open behind her. Not because every door should remain open, but because the people inside had chosen that one.
